gaps.currentBehavior: The committed application graph is a hyperedge array plus a separate graphIdentity. App.jsx always serializes it to CANDY as graphType Hypergraph. DynamicHypergraph, OrdinaryGraph, and DynamicOrdinaryGraph exist only in lower-level contracts/tests and are not selectable authoritative application states.
gaps.desiredBehavior: A single authoritative graph envelope carries graphType, graphId, graphVersion, graphFingerprint, and committed hyperedges; DynamicHypergraph is explicitly created or selected and is observable by UI, Assistant, and Runtime without inference.
gaps.rootCause: The application graph model predates the CANDY graph-type contract and graphType was hard-coded at the integration boundary.
gaps.authorityImpact: Without an application-owned type, CUDA_INCREMENTAL is intentionally unreachable and lower-level type names cannot grant authority.
gaps.securityImpact: Inferring DynamicHypergraph would wrongly expand executable capability; hard-coding Hypergraph safely blocks it but prevents Scope 5.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Type-only transitions are not included in the current fingerprint/version transition.

gaps.currentBehavior: The application has batch-preview state and staged Assistant GraphMutationPlan confirmations, but no authoritative pending DynamicHypergraph update record, update status, revision, digest, or owner.
gaps.desiredBehavior: One application-owned pending-update aggregate represents draft, validated, analysis, apply, stale, discarded, and terminal states without mutating the committed graph.
gaps.rootCause: Scope 4C deliberately accepted pendingUpdate only as an injected hook input and did not create an application authoring workflow.
gaps.authorityImpact: There is no object that can safely authorize incremental analysis or later application.
gaps.securityImpact: Ad hoc pending objects would create replay and substitution opportunities.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Batch preview, conversational pending action, and Runtime pendingUpdate are overlapping concepts with no common lifecycle.

gaps.currentBehavior: GraphMutationPlan supports rich graph edits while HypergraphMotifUpdate supports only whole-hyperedge deletions and insertions under DELETE_THEN_INSERT. No application adapter derives the latter from the former or from the validated preview diff.
gaps.desiredBehavior: The pending aggregate retains GraphMutationPlan as authoring/apply authority and deterministically derives one immutable HypergraphMotifUpdate transport projection from committed-versus-proposed incidence.
gaps.rootCause: The generic mutation workflow and qualified motif update contract were developed independently.
gaps.authorityImpact: The model or UI must not construct trusted Runtime updates directly.
gaps.securityImpact: A deterministic diff prevents omitted affected edges, collision bypass, and model-crafted transport fields.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Incidence changes, replacements, and metadata-only edits need one unambiguous net effect.

gaps.currentBehavior: Generic batch and conversational commits can mutate the graph after confirmation, but there is no applyPendingHypergraphUpdate operation that consumes an exact pending revision, revalidates it, verifies the proposed fingerprint, commits once, clears authority, and re-observes state.
gaps.desiredBehavior: A single atomic application action rechecks base identity/version/fingerprint, plan hash, update digest, proposed graph fingerprint, and next version immediately before commit; analysis remains optional and never applies.
gaps.authorityImpact: Application authority is currently separate from the Runtime result, which is safe but incomplete.
gaps.securityImpact: A dedicated consume-once action is required to prevent stale confirmation and apply-after-supersession.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: The committed graph and nextGraphVersion can otherwise diverge.

gaps.currentBehavior: The browser graph fingerprint is a short FNV-derived content marker that excludes graphType. The Runtime binds graph/update artifacts by SHA-256, but the pending proposed graph has no application-level digest/fingerprint binding and the current graph fingerprint is not carried into the motif result binding.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Graph type participates in authority; pending updates bind base graph ID/version/fingerprint, immutable update digest/revision, next version, and proposed graph fingerprint. Runtime artifacts remain SHA-256 authorities.
gaps.rootCause: UI stale-state identity and Runtime artifact identity are separate layers with no Scope-5 bridge.
gaps.authorityImpact: The application cannot prove that an accepted delta still describes the preview proposed for application.
gaps.securityImpact: Missing type/proposed-state binding enables stale or substituted state if future UI state is wired naively.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Type-only changes and proposed-graph edits may not invalidate all dependent state.

gaps.currentBehavior: updateId is bounded and result-bound but is not required to be unique or content-addressed. Runtime duplicate suppression uses the full request hash, not updateId, and failed/cancelled requests may be resubmitted.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Every material edit creates a fresh update revision and digest; a consumed/discarded/superseded update ID cannot regain authority, and duplicate IDs with different digests are rejected.
gaps.rootCause: Lower-level contracts treat updateId as a label because they are stateless execution contracts.
gaps.authorityImpact: Update lifecycle, rather than Runtime execution, must own consume/supersede semantics.
gaps.securityImpact: Prevents update-ID replay and confirmation reuse across edited content.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Multiple semantic updates cannot be confused under one label.
testsRequired: duplicate update ID same digest idempotence

gaps.currentBehavior: Runtime motif execution has an expensive-compute confirmation and generic graph mutation application has a graph-edit confirmation. There are no Scope-5 action types or tokens for pending-update staging/editing versus analysis versus application.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Editing/staging remains non-committing; analysis confirmation binds the exact update and Runtime session; apply confirmation separately binds the exact pending revision and proposed graph. Neither confirmation is reusable after edits, graph replacement, cancellation, timeout, or session change.
gaps.rootCause: No first-class pending update exists to bind into the confirmation registry.
gaps.authorityImpact: Analysis and application must remain independent authorized actions.
gaps.securityImpact: Prevents confirmation replay and implicit apply/run coupling.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Stale UI actions cannot commit or execute a changed update.

gaps.currentBehavior: Incremental results are truthfully rendered as signed delta-only values. The hook stores only one selected result and clears it on context changes, so there is no authoritative prior-static-count registry and no safe before/delta/after reconstruction.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Always show signed deltas by class and total. Reconstruct after counts only from a validated static result bound to the exact base graph/taxonomy plus a validated delta bound to the exact pending update; label reconstruction as derived and reject stale/mismatched prior results.
gaps.authorityImpact: A prior count must never be inferred from UI history or conversation.
gaps.securityImpact: Prevents fabricated absolute counts and cross-graph result composition.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Derived totals must remain version/taxonomy consistent and nonnegative.

gaps.currentBehavior: The browser validates runtimeSessionId, jobId, requestId, algorithm, taxonomy, backend, mode, graph/update artifact IDs, graph/update refs, request digest, result artifact digest, CUDA device, and execution metadata. Bindings live only in an in-memory job map and do not include proposed graph fingerprint or an application pending-update revision.
gaps.desiredBehavior: An accepted Scope-5 result is attached only to the exact pending revision and proposed graph; reopening after reload or Runtime restart is non-authoritative unless all bindings are freshly re-established.
gaps.rootCause: Scope 4C had no application update object to bind.
gaps.authorityImpact: Validated execution identity is necessary but not sufficient for later graph application.
gaps.securityImpact: Prevents result and artifact substitution across pending updates.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Only current pending state may display an actionable/current delta.

gaps.currentBehavior: The Runtime serializes motif jobs and the browser rejects stale context during upload/open, but there is no application policy for a second pending update, automatic supersession, cancel/timeout invalidation of apply confirmation, or a browser reload during a running job.
gaps.desiredBehavior: At most one authoritative pending update exists; creating/editing another supersedes the old revision, marks old jobs/results stale, and invalidates confirmations. Cancellation/timeout never applies, and any later apply requires a fresh independent confirmation and current-state recheck.
gaps.rootCause: Job lifecycle and graph-edit lifecycle are currently independent.
gaps.authorityImpact: Job completion cannot grant apply authority.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Concurrent edits cannot race a result into the current workspace.

gaps.currentBehavior: Statistics exposes STATIC only; Runtime panel has an incremental button gated by DynamicHypergraph plus pendingUpdateContext, but that state is unreachable. The Assistant infers INCREMENTAL from request wording, not from graph type alone, which is safe.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Central rules select STATIC only for explicit current-count requests and INCREMENTAL only for explicit change/delta requests with a validated current pending update and exact qualified capability; user choice is visible and no fallback occurs.
gaps.rootCause: Scope 4C supplied safety gates but not a complete product workflow.
gaps.authorityImpact: DynamicHypergraph alone must never authorize INCREMENTAL.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Avoids analyzing the wrong state or presenting the wrong result type.

gaps.currentBehavior: Batch Updates previews a temporary full-graph overlay and can commit/discard. CANDY panels can render signed deltas. No UI identifies a graph as DynamicHypergraph, shows a durable pending update, edits/discards it, explains stale state, or exposes a separate Apply action.
gaps.desiredBehavior: A minimal update panel reuses Batch Updates and Preview, shows base/next identity and lifecycle, exposes validate/edit/discard, stages incremental analysis, renders signed deltas, and places Apply behind a distinct confirmation.
gaps.rootCause: No application state exists for UI binding.
gaps.authorityImpact: UI must distinguish preview, analysis, and application.
gaps.securityImpact: Clear stale/authority copy reduces accidental execution and apply confusion.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Users need a single visible source of truth for pending state.

gaps.currentBehavior: The Assistant can create and confirm generic graph mutation plans and can request incremental motif analysis only if a pendingUpdateContext already exists. It cannot create/edit/discard/apply a Scope-5 pending update as typed capabilities.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Existing typed graph actions stage the pending update; new bounded capabilities manage its lifecycle and apply it. The model only selects IDs/actions and never supplies trusted Runtime graph/update bodies.
gaps.rootCause: Scope 4C intentionally stopped at bounded Runtime analysis selectors.
gaps.authorityImpact: The model remains an untrusted selector; application code owns update construction and confirmation.
gaps.securityImpact: Prevents model-crafted update artifacts and direct application.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Assistant observation must include bounded revision/digest/status and re-observe after every action.

gaps.currentBehavior: Thread persistence intentionally restores only inert references, sets graph.available false, and drops pendingAction. Graph contents, CANDY job bindings, results, and pending updates are not persisted. The pairing token is sessionStorage-only.
gaps.desiredBehavior: Conservative default: do not restore execution/apply authority. If descriptive pending-update metadata is persisted, it reloads as STALE_REVIEW_REQUIRED with no confirmation/job/result authority and must be rebound to a freshly loaded exact graph.
gaps.rootCause: Scope 5 persistence semantics are unspecified; existing persistence correctly rejects executable restoration.
gaps.authorityImpact: Storage must never recreate execution authority.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Reloaded descriptions cannot masquerade as current graph state.

gaps.currentBehavior: Qualified transport limits are strong, but the browser computes contextKey by JSON-stringifying graph plus pending update and uploads base64 copies. The UI does not expose the 256-hyperedge/100000-incidence/2MiB packed incremental constraints before confirmation, and Runtime request/artifact limits are looser than native motif limits.
gaps.desiredBehavior: A shared preflight reports exact qualified motif/update limits before staging; update derivation is bounded before cloning; the UI explains infeasibility without uploading or model/native execution.
gaps.rootCause: Limits are enforced across adapter, packer, Runtime, and Preview layers but not presented as one application policy.
gaps.authorityImpact: Preflight is advisory until the same limits are rechecked at submission.
gaps.securityImpact: Reduces browser memory/CPU denial-of-service from oversized updates.

gaps.currentBehavior: Scope 4A/4B/4C and post-diagnosis tests cover contracts, native parity, Runtime boundaries, UI truthfulness, confirmation, and generic mutation safety, but none exercise a real first-class application DynamicHypergraph pending-update lifecycle.
gaps.desiredBehavior: A layered Scope-5 suite covers contracts, state reducer, adapters, UI, Assistant, persistence, races, real Runtime/CUDA, browser behavior, and security regression while retaining all frozen backend qualifications.
gaps.rootCause: The application workflow does not exist yet.
gaps.authorityImpact: No Scope-5 authority claim can be qualified without end-to-end tests.
gaps.securityImpact: Replay, stale-state, substitution, and race properties require explicit negative coverage.
gaps.stateIntegrityImpact: Every transition and terminal state needs invariant checks.
